rules: P2 DECISION-AUTHORITY.md §3 A1-A9 with the §5 v0.2 changes C1-C5

decisions.statement: The `reminders <date>` command computes each appointment's reminder time under DEC-C08 (48 hours before the appointment), because CLIN-51-R1 requires the reminder decision in force and DEC-C08 is accepted and supersedes DEC-C06; the R1 example (run on 2026-03-10 lists appointments on 2026-03-12) agrees. This chooses against the current Rules.reminderAt/reminderLeadHours, which still implement the superseded DEC-C06 (24 hours). The DEC-C08 lead time is added in Rules as its own rule naming DEC-C08, per docs/architecture.md (rules live only in Rules).
reasons: A2 'docs/architecture.md' does not resolve to a requirement, decision record or approval

decisions.statement: The existing `reminder <appointment>` command and its 24-hour output are left unchanged, since the acceptance criteria say existing behaviour is unchanged except as the requirements say and CLIN-51 only specifies the new `reminders` command. UNRESOLVED QUESTION for Patient Services: `reminder <appointment>` still follows the superseded DEC-C06 (24 h) and will now disagree with `reminders <date>` (DEC-C08, 48 h); should `reminder` also be moved to DEC-C08? Not changed without authorization.

An appointment's reminder is 'sent on' a date when the calendar date of its reminder date-time (appointment date-time minus the DEC-C08 lead) equals that date. Only appointments currently in state are considered (cancel removes appointments, so cancelled ones are never listed). Output is `reminders on <yyyy-MM-dd>: <id> at <yyyy-MM-dd> <HH:mm>, ...` with entries joined by ", ", or `reminders on <yyyy-MM-dd>: none`. The command returns the state unchanged.

Entries are ordered by appointment date then time; appointments at the same date and time (different clinicians) are ordered by appointment id, mirroring the existing `schedule` command's (Time, Id) ordering. No source gives a tie-break; open to correction.
decisions.notAuthorized: Entries are ordered by appointment date then time; appointments at the same date and time (different clinicians) are ordered by appointment id, mirroring the existing `schedule` command's (Time, Id) ordering. No source gives a tie-break; open to correction.
reasons: A6 an `default-rule` decision needs an accepted decision record, a granted approval, or a revision by the owner of every source it changes; requirements of other owners, notes and code cannot authorize it

decisions.statement: Argument errors reuse existing conventions: a malformed date gives `error: invalid date <text>` via Commands.parseDate, and a wrong number of arguments gives `error: usage: reminders <date>` via the existing usage lookup. Either way state is unchanged (README Errors).

Add `reminders <date>` to Cli.usage immediately after `reminder <appointment>`, so `help` lists it there. Note: usageOf matches `reminder` against `reminder <appointment>` first, so `reminder` usage errors stay unchanged.

Add acceptance tests in tests/Clinic.Tests/Acceptance/CLIN51AcceptanceTests.fs for criteria the provided tests do not cover: the R1 listing example (two appointments in time order), state unchanged after the command, and invalid-date error.
